implementation_notes: In the Scala stack the endpoint becomes a stream stage: Alpakka's AmqpSource.atMostOnceSource(NamedQueueSourceSettings(...), bufferSize) turns a queue into a Source of ReadResult (committableSource variants expose CommittableReadResult with ack/nack), while AmqpSink.simple / AmqpFlow.withConfirm handle publishing. The classic endpoint class is replaced by graph composition with explicit back-pressure (bufferSize, confirmation timeouts); an explicit endpoint object remains justified when several streams share one connection lifecycle or when the surrounding system is not stream-based.
code_sketch:
val settings = NamedQueueSourceSettings(AmqpUriConnectionProvider("amqp://localhost:5672"), "orders")
val done: Future[Done] =
  AmqpSource.atMostOnceSource(settings, bufferSize = 10)
    .map(msg => handle(msg.bytes.utf8String))
    .runWith(Sink.ignore)
pitfalls: A source materializes its own connection per stage unless you wrap the provider in AmqpCachedConnectionProvider; recreated graphs can leak connections otherwise.
A failed stage stops the whole graph: without restart logic (or a supervising stream), the endpoint stops consuming after the first error.
atMostOnceSource acknowledges without waiting for handling - use committableSource when the handler may fail and redelivery matters.
